Attached is NTWKTech's annotated DPA (redline). Key items our privacy counsel flagged:

- Liability: we can’t accept a broad indemnity for third-party data breaches.

Please confirm Redwood's stance on SCCs vs. alternatives, and whether you can provide SOC 2 evidence and a subprocessor addendum instead of prior consent.

Laura — thanks for the redline and clear callouts. Looping in Karthik from Legal and David from Solutions so we can provide technical and legal responses.

Quick answers up front:
- SCCs are acceptable: Redwood typically executes SCCs with an EU Annex (we also have a UK addendum). Karthik can confirm the exact clause language we propose.
- SOC 2: we can provide a SOC 2 Type II report under NDA; I'll ask our security team to share the artifact link.
- Subprocessors: we'll provide the current subprocessor list. TelemetryCloud is on the list but only processes aggregated, non-identifiable metrics; David can confirm retention/PI details.
- Retention: 12-month max for logs is a reasonable starting point; we need to align on what constitutes "logs" vs. audit traces.

Next steps: Karthik — can you do a short pass on the liability and transfer language and propose carrierable alternative wording? David, can you confirm TelemetryCloud's data handling and retention (and whether it crosses EU borders)?

Subject: Re: NTWKTech – DPA redline (initial)

Laura / Hannah — thanks, I did a first-pass legal response and attached a marked-up counter (Redwood_DPA_Response_20260213.docx). Summary of our positions:

1) Transfer mechanism: we will accept SCCs and will provide an EU Annex and UK Addendum. We'll also include a statement about our technical and organizational measures in Annex B; see attached "SCCs_AnnexB_v2.pdf" for the proposed language.

2) Subprocessors: Redwood maintains a published list of subprocessors and will notify customers 30 days before onboarding any new subprocessor. For TelemetryCloud: they process aggregated telemetry (no customer prompt text), are SOC 2 Type II, and host in us-west and eu-west regions depending on job. David/Grace — please confirm whether any raw prompt data is routed to TelemetryCloud (I expect not).

3) Retention: we can accept a 12-month default for transient logs but must carve out (a) aggregated telemetry and (b) system logs required for security investigations. We'll add a clause obligating Redwood to provide reasonable justification when retaining beyond 12 months.

4) Liability/indemnity: we can't accept open-ended indemnities tied to third-party breaches; propose a mutually acceptable cap and carveouts tied to willful misconduct.

5) Evidence: we will provide SOC 2 Type II + pen test summary under NDA and can include redacted reports in the Drive folder.

If NTWKTech can accept SCCs + our proposed notification model for subprocessors (rather than prior written consent), we can prepare a DocuSign package with the EU Annex and the DPA for signature.

-Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Response_20260213.docx

From: Mark Hollis <mhollis@firmlaw.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Kim <laura.kim@ntwktech.com>, contracts@ntwktech.com
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: NTWKTech – DPA redline (initial)

Karthik / Hannah — thanks for the quick turn. A few inline responses from our side:

- SCCs + EU Annex: acceptable in principle. We'll need to review your AnnexB wording but ok to proceed to DocuSign once we have the SOC 2 evidence.

- Subprocessors: NTWKTech cannot accept a model that permits post-hoc notification for any processor that accesses customer prompt content. For processors that only see aggregate telemetry we can accept notification, but for processors that may process customer data we require prior notice plus the right to object. Please confirm TelemetryCloud's access level in writing.

- Retention: we can accept a 12-month cap, but carveouts for security are limited to 90 days unless otherwise approved; propose Redwood provide a retention proposal for security logs.

- Liability: NTWKTech cannot accept language that limits liability for data breaches caused by Redwood's negligence. We need clearer carveouts or minimum liability for breach events.

If we can resolve the subprocessor access (TelemetryCloud) and agree on the security log retention window, we're prepared to move to DocuSign this week.

On a procedural note: please provide the SOC 2 under NDA (we have an NDA executed with Hannah's team) and upload any redacted reports to the Drive link prior to signature.

Regards,
Mark Hollis
Partner, FirmLaw LLP
